chunks: From him, from Safwan and Fadala together, from al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both), who said:

I asked him about a man who had intercourse with his slave-girl, and her menstruation was delayed, and he feared that she might have become pregnant, so he dedicated to Allah the freeing of a slave, fasting, and charity, if she menstruates. The slave-girl had menstruated before he swore the oath by a day or two, and he did not know. He said: 'There is no obligation upon him.'

key_terms.لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ شَيْءٌ: there is no obligation upon him

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a vow made based on a condition that has already occurred but was unknown to the vow-maker?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the ruling of *Nadhr al-Gharam* (vow of expiation) when the condition is fulfilled prior to the vow due to the vow-maker's ignorance (*jahil*). The Imam (peace be upon him) rules that since the girl had already menstruated before the vow was made, the condition was not truly contingent on future uncertainty, thereby exempting the man from the obligation of freeing a slave, fasting, or giving charity. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that a vow requires a genuine contingency; if the event has already occurred, the vow is effectively void unless specified otherwise.
